name: Hartford
summary: Connecticut's capital — Mark Twain's whimsical mansion, the oldest public art museum in America, and a gold-domed statehouse.

lodging.name: A downtown Hartford hotel
lodging.blurb: Central to the capitol, Bushnell Park, and the museums.

foodMustTry.name: A New Haven-style apizza run (or wait a day)
foodMustTry.blurb: Connecticut's famous coal-fired pizza is 40 minutes south — save room.

days.label: Day 58 — Twain & the Atheneum
days.summary: A literary house and America's first public art museum.

item.title: The Mark Twain House & Museum
item.blurb: The eccentric Gilded-Age mansion where Twain wrote Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn, beside Harriet Beecher Stowe's house.

item.title: The Wadsworth Atheneum
item.blurb: The oldest continuously operating public art museum in the country, opened in 1844 — Hudson River School landscapes, Colt firearms, and a Caravaggio.

item.title: The Connecticut State Capitol
item.blurb: A wild marble-and-granite pile above Bushnell Park, gold-domed and covered in gables and statuary — one architecture critic called it the handsomest capitol in America and Mark Twain, who lived up the road, reportedly called it something less kind. Free tours, and the Genius of Connecticut stands in the atrium.

days.label: Day 59 — Down to New Haven
days.summary: A short hop to Yale and the pizza capital.
